advanced_notes.ACID: Full ACID transaction semantics are a major differentiator for ingestion safety.
advanced_notes.GRAFBLAS: Neo4j is credited for mature graph algorithms via GDS, not for being GRAFBLAS-native.
advanced_notes.UDFs: Custom procedures/functions are a mature extension path.
advanced_notes.concurrent_writes: Transactional writes complete without lost increments in the 3-writer harness.
advanced_notes.multi_process: Documented client/server architecture supports concurrent client processes.

concurrent_write_metrics.notes: Offline shared-counter harness: 3 parallel writers x 100 writes each.

cons: Heavier service footprint than LadybugDB or FalkorDB.
Licensing and product packaging need review before production procurement.
candidates.deployment_notes: Use DB_HOST/DB_PORT with Bolt defaults. Keep real DB connections disabled in CI unless explicitly authorized.
candidates.name: Neo4j
pros: Strongest combined evidence for concurrent writes, transactions, UDFs, and multi-process clients.
Mature Python driver and broad operational documentation reduce unattended-agent risk.
Graph Data Science ecosystem covers the graph algorithm need even though it is not exactly GRAFBLAS-native.
candidates.summary: Best M066 production candidate after advanced criteria: mature ACID transactions, UDF/procedure support, documented multi-client safety, and strong graph algorithm ecosystem outweigh heavier operations.

advanced_notes.ACID: Atomic command execution is useful, but this is not a full multi-statement ACID transaction surface.
advanced_notes.GRAFBLAS: FalkorDB inherits GraphBLAS-oriented execution from RedisGraph lineage.
advanced_notes.UDFs: Custom extension paths exist around Redis modules, but query-level UDF ergonomics are limited.
advanced_notes.concurrent_writes: Server-side serialization avoids lost writes in the 3-writer harness.
advanced_notes.multi_process: Multiple clients can target the server safely for normal writes.

concurrent_write_metrics.notes: Offline shared-counter harness: 3 parallel writers x 100 writes each.

cons: UDF path is limited compared with Neo4j procedures or PostgreSQL functions.
Transaction semantics are not as broad as mature ACID database engines.
candidates.deployment_notes: Use DB_HOST/DB_PORT for local service discovery. Offline benchmark mode keeps network access disabled by default.
candidates.name: FalkorDB
pros: Native graph-vector positioning stays close to the M063 hybrid workload.
Redis-like operational model keeps deployment simpler than JVM or PostgreSQL extension stacks.
GraphBLAS lineage directly addresses the advanced graph algorithm concern.
candidates.summary: Strong graph-vector fit with server-side serialized writes and GraphBLAS lineage, but weaker UDF and full transaction depth than Neo4j or PostgreSQL-backed AGE.

advanced_notes.ACID: Full PostgreSQL ACID transactions directly address write safety.
advanced_notes.GRAFBLAS: No first-class GRAFBLAS support is credited for AGE itself.
advanced_notes.UDFs: PostgreSQL function and extension support earns a full UDF score.
advanced_notes.concurrent_writes: PostgreSQL-backed serialization avoids lost writes in the harness.
advanced_notes.multi_process: Mature multi-process client/server semantics are a major strength.

concurrent_write_metrics.notes: Offline shared-counter harness: 3 parallel writers x 100 writes each.

cons: Graph-vector capability is a composed AGE plus vector-extension stack, not native AGE alone.
Graph algorithms are not GRAFBLAS-native in this evaluation.
Deployment is more complex than a Python-native library.
candidates.deployment_notes: Use DB_HOST/DB_PORT with PostgreSQL defaults. Production import is not authorized in this offline benchmark.
candidates.name: Apache AGE
pros: PostgreSQL transaction semantics and process safety directly address ingestion concerns.
UDF support is mature through PostgreSQL functions and extensions.
Operational consolidation with future PostgreSQL work remains attractive.
candidates.summary: Best consolidation option if PostgreSQL becomes the dominant architecture constraint; advanced write/transaction/UDF scores improve its ranking despite weaker native graph-vector ergonomics.

advanced_notes.ACID: No full transactional database contract is credited for production concurrent ingestion.
advanced_notes.GRAFBLAS: No first-class GRAFBLAS graph algorithm support is credited in this evaluation.
advanced_notes.UDFs: Python extensibility helps, but it is not equivalent to database-managed UDFs.
advanced_notes.concurrent_writes: The offline unsafe read-modify-write harness records lost writes, representing the unresolved multi-writer concern.
advanced_notes.multi_process: Multi-process safety remains an open risk without an external coordinator.

concurrent_write_metrics.notes: Offline shared-counter harness: 3 parallel writers x 100 writes each.

cons: No clear GraphBLAS algorithm surface was found in the local vendor-source reference.
Concurrent multi-writer semantics are not strong enough for production ingestion without an external lock or queue.
Advanced feature documentation is too thin for a binding production choice.
candidates.deployment_notes: Treat as a prototype/intermediate candidate unless a later slice proves external serialization, process safety, and failure recovery.
candidates.name: LadybugDB
pros: Best migration ergonomics from the current Python graph layer.
Python-native development model is easy to inspect and test offline.
Hybrid graph-vector positioning remains attractive for scientific KG prototyping.
candidates.summary: Still the lowest migration-cost option from NetworkX, but the new advanced criteria expose material risk around concurrent writers, GraphBLAS coverage, and ACID semantics.

advanced_notes.ACID: Partial transaction confidence only; live durability proof is still needed.
advanced_notes.GRAFBLAS: No first-class GRAFBLAS support is credited.
advanced_notes.UDFs: Extension surface is not mature enough for high score.
advanced_notes.concurrent_writes: Optimistic serialized harness succeeds, but production semantics need live-server proof.
advanced_notes.multi_process: Credited as plausible client/server safety, not yet proven for daily-archive ingestion.

concurrent_write_metrics.notes: Offline shared-counter harness: 3 parallel writers x 100 writes each.

cons: Python integration and production history are less mature than Neo4j, FalkorDB, or AGE.
No credited GRAFBLAS support and weak UDF evidence.
candidates.deployment_notes: Keep as a watch-list candidate; do not use for production import until live concurrency and recovery evidence exists.
candidates.name: HelixDB
pros: Strong graph-vector product direction for agentic KG workloads.
Rust implementation may become attractive for performance-sensitive paths.
candidates.summary: Interesting graph-vector system for future review, but current Python maturity, advanced documentation, and GraphBLAS/UDF evidence are not enough to win M066.
